newsitem.title: UK: Xmas will not be boom for UK retailers - survey.
newsitem.headline: Xmas will not be boom for UK retailers - survey.

text.p: Christmas trade in Britain might not be a boom, but it will be the best for eight years, according to research from independent consultants Verdict.
Verdict said official figures for November sales showed a slowing in consumer demand, causing a certain amount of nervousness among retailers.
"However, research released by Verdict...suggests that there might not be a boom, but trade will still be the best for eight years."
More than one fifth of shoppers interviewed by Verdict felt able to spend more this Christmas, while a third had not started their Christmas shopping as late as December 10.
Verdict expects retail sales to be worth just under 20 billion pounds for December, up 7.7 percent on last year and the best level of trade since 1988.
Verdict found that not all retailers would share in the upturn. Clothing seemed to be a patchy sector and a number of retailers had introduced Christmas sales to entice shoppers.
The drinks trade might suffer from cross-Channel business, as some 16 percent surveyed said they had bought drinks abroad for Christmas.
The survey showed that shoppers were not particularly loyal to their superstores, despite the introduction of loyalty cards.
"Only 58 percent of those canvassed said they would be using the same supermarket for the food buying this Christmas as last year."
